notes.summary: FlexPart is a unified image-to-3D part-generation model accepting variable-granularity geometric conditions (sparse points, bounding boxes, masks) via gated adaptive modulation, plus asymmetric geometric guidance for cross-granularity consistency. On PartVerseXL with mask conditioning it cuts Part CD by 16.6% vs TripoSG+SAM3D and 10.5% vs OmniPart while keeping whole-mesh quality.
notes.why: Direct hit on the user's 3D generation interest, with a controllable/editing-flavored design and released code.

notes.summary: SpectralCanary audits whether a T2I model was fine-tuned on a specific dataset by low-pass-blending a fixed canary image into every collection image, then verifying the transferred signal in model outputs. It reaches 91.1% per-generation TPR@1% FPR across tests, preserves image fidelity (SSIM 0.989), and resists removal attacks without aggressive distortion.
notes.why: A practical, deployable proactive dataset-use auditing tool squarely in the user's AI copyright policy / dataset watermarking facet.

notes.summary: BrickWright shows that frontier coding agents, given a Python brick-assembly toolkit (BrickLayer) plus a physical-feasibility validator with feedback, can produce physically valid LEGO builds from text or image prompts. Validity jumps from 9-69% for baseline agents to 100% on 512 prompts while outperforming specialized text-to-brick models.
notes.why: An agentic coding-and-tooling system that also touches 3D generation, bridging the user's top two interests.

notes.summary: The paper introduces a thought-pruning method for test-time reasoning that directly optimizes pass@k over the selected partial-solution pool, naturally balancing quality and diversity instead of tuning them separately. Across eight open-weight reasoning models it outperforms existing quality- and diversity-based pruning, especially when keeping a moderate number of candidates.
notes.why: Not agent-specific, but a solid test-time-compute technique relevant to scaling agent reasoning and evaluation.

notes.why: Adjacent to the agent-benchmarks facet: a cheap proxy evaluation method for embodied agent capability.
